# 4. Starting

## 4.1 A first program

```
>10 FOR I%=1 TO 10
>20   PRINT I%, I%*I%
>30 NEXT
>RUN
```

Lines with a number go into the program; lines without run at once.
`LIST` shows the program, `NEW` clears it. How lines are typed and
edited: chapter 5.

## 4.2 Saving and loading

Programs are saved in the current directory of the Ultimate's file
system (chapter 7):

```
*DIR /SD/myprogs
SAVE "SQUARES"
LOAD "SQUARES"
CHAIN "SQUARES"
```

## 4.3 The keyboard

#### `KEYBOARD`

Letters type in capitals, as with CAPS LOCK on a BBC Micro; Shift gives lower case. Shift+C= switches CAPS LOCK off and on again: off, letters type in lower case and Shift gives capitals (BASIC's keywords are capitals). OSBYTE &CA reads and sets it (bit 4 = 1: off), as on the BBC.

The ASCII characters the C64 keyboard lacks:

```
\  pound key       ^  up-arrow
_  left-arrow      |  Shift+pound
~  Shift+up-arrow  {  Shift++
}  Shift+-         `  Shift+@
```

RUN/STOP is ESCAPE: it stops a program or a listing. RESTORE also sets ESCAPE.

Lines are typed with the MOS line editor (*EDIT), in every screen mode, up to 238 characters:

```
LEFT, RIGHT     move in the line
CLR/HOME        start of the line
Shift+CLR/HOME  end of the line
DEL, INST       delete, insert space
UP, DOWN        earlier lines typed
CTRL+cursor     move the copy cursor
F1              COPY
RETURN          enter the line
```

COPY editing as on a BBC Micro: CTRL with a cursor key starts a second cursor and moves it over the screen; F1 copies the character under it into the line and moves it on, so a listed line can be copied, in every mode (in the bitmap modes the character is recognised from its pixels, as on a BBC Micro; the 4-pixel modes 0, 1 and 3 need the REU's 4x6 font for that). UP and DOWN go through the last 127 lines typed at the prompt (kept in the REU). *EDIT C64 brings back the C64 screen editor (move the cursor anywhere and press RETURN; 78 characters after the prompt).

GET and INKEY return the cursor keys as 136-139 (left, right, down, up), DEL as 127 and CLR as 12.
